title: order: one order for one unit, as saved games and issue_orders write it
description: unit is "task_force:N", "air_group:N" or "land_unit:N". The body's kind must be one of that kind of unit's: a task force's are set_route, set_speed, set_mission, load, unload, set_rules_of_engagement, set_home_port, detach, set_readiness and send_to_yard (no other key); load takes an optional unit, a land unit written "land_unit:N"; an air group's are set_air_mission, set_search_arc, set_patrol_share, set_rest_threshold, set_reach, set_target_priority and rebase; a land unit's are set_posture (posture defend or attack, a standing order) and march (hex [q, r], a standing order until the unit arrives). The decoder checks the pairing; the schema checks the fields of each kind. Every quantity is a decimal string, every count a whole number. waypoints are [q, r] pairs. A load names no cargo for supply; with a unit it may name cargo supply, fuel or none.

act_at.description: Optional (decision 0096): [q, r] hexes, each one of the waypoints, to act at. A force halts at a marked waypoint if it has work there (a bombardment or cargo) and steams on when the work is done. The last waypoint needs no mark. A mark that is not one of the waypoints is refused.

cargo.description: What is loaded: supply or fuel. "none" is for a load with a unit and loads the unit's men only; a load with no unit that names "none" is refused as malformed.

unit.description: A land unit of the side, written land_unit:N in the side's own numbering (decision 0066, 5): the load then takes the unit's men ashore in the force's hex aboard first and the cargo after. With a unit and no cargo key the cargo is supply. In a saved game the number is the engine's. The decoder checks the form land_unit:N.

hex.description: The coast hex the landing is for, [q, r] (decision 0095, 1).

roster.description: The land units that are to land from the force, each written "land_unit:N". May be empty.

mission.description: What the group does each daylight pulse, and only that: rest (stays on the ground); search (flies the arc set by set_search_arc, and flies nothing if none is set); naval_strike (the staff launches it, in the same pulse, at an enemy contact the side holds that was reported in that pulse or the one before and lies within the aircraft type's strike radius); combat_air_patrol (fighters: a share stays over their own hex as patrol, the rest escort a raid within their radius). Set missions before the contact appears: search, the strike decision and the strike all happen inside one day, and a group flies only the mission it is on. For a strike on a base use base_strike with target_base.

base_strike: in the morning pulse, with no contact needed, the group launches at the named enemy base if the base is held by the other side and within the aircraft type's strike radius, and its bombs can hit aircraft on the ground and supply there.

target_base.description: The number of an enemy base, as list_bases gives it under enemy_bases.

from_deg.description: Bearing in degrees where the arc starts: 0 is north (up the map, toward smaller r), 90 east, 180 south, 270 west. A multiple of 10 from 0 to 350. The arc runs clockwise from from_deg to to_deg.

to_deg.description: Bearing in degrees where the arc ends, going clockwise from from_deg; a multiple of 10 from 0 to 350. from_deg 270 and to_deg 90 is the northern half; equal bearings mean the whole circle. Arcs wider than 180 degrees are allowed.

range_nm.description: How far out the group searches, in miles: above 0 and at most the aircraft type's search range (a longer range is refused, and the refusal names the maximum). A longer range costs more wear. Search does nothing until an arc is set; the arc stays until another is set.

share.description: The share of the group kept over its own hex, from "0" to "1". "1" keeps every fighter at home and sends no escort; "0.5" keeps half and lets half escort raids; "0" keeps none at home and sends all as escort.

reach.description: "normal" (the default): strikes and escorts go as far as the aircraft type's strike radius. "extended": a share more than the radius (the air combat figures' extended_reach_share, 0.25 as shipped, so a type with a radius of 250 miles reaches 312), at the price that an aircraft that flew beyond its radius may run out of fuel and come down in the sea on the way home, and its crew may be lost. Extended reach is refused where the scenario has no air combat figures.

kinds.description: The kinds of ship the group's strikes go for, in order, first choice first: at least one, none named twice. A naval_strike group launches only at a contact taken for a kind on this list, the kind earliest on it first, then the nearest; a contact of any other kind is never launched at, so a short list holds the strike back. Over the target the group attacks the ship of the force found that ranks first by the list, kinds not on it following in the order carrier, battleship, cruiser, destroyer, transport, auxiliary. The default is all six kinds in that order. The list is a standing order: it stays until another replaces it.

base.description: The number of a base of your side, other than the one the group is at, within the group's transfer range: twice the longer of its aircraft type's search range and strike radius. Not a standing order: it is done at the start of the day and spent. The group flies nothing that day, and its damaged aircraft are written off at the base it leaves. Not for a group aboard a ship.

posture.description: defend or attack (decision 0090, 1, 2). A standing order: the unit keeps the posture until another order replaces it, or until a tired unit on attack goes back to defend and the order is spent. Refused for a unit that is not yours, a destroyed unit and a unit with no man ashore.

hex.description: The hex to march the unit's men ashore to, [q, r] (decision 0094, 3): a neighbour of the unit's hex joined to it by a land link, which the unit's line lists as march_to. A pair of whole numbers. The unit's own hex stops a march. A standing order until the unit arrives or another march order replaces it. Refused for a unit that is not yours, a destroyed unit, a unit with no man ashore, and a hex no land link joins to the unit's.

activity.description: What the unit does on a day it does not march or fight (decision 4 of 0099 and 4 of 0097): ready (rehearses if it is on the roster of a force preparing a landing) or train. A standing order.
